Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 5-day history of dry cough and profuse runny nose in a woman with diabetes and hypertension; advised supportive care and safety-netting for probable viral chest infection.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 5 days of dry cough (every 20–30 minutes) and constant rhinorrhea with green discharge.
- Associated symptoms: Feels hot with intermittent chills; myalgias. No measured temperature. Early transient diarrhea at onset (now resolved). Eating/drinking okay; normal urination. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, pleuritic pain, hemoptysis, epistaxis, rash, headache, or vision changes. No sinus pain reported.
- Pertinent negatives: No current vomiting or diarrhea. No chronic lung disease or frequent chest infections. Wheeze only with intense exercise.
- Past medical history: Diabetes mellitus (type not specified). Hypertension.
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented). Lisinopril “two hundred” (dose/route/frequency not documented). OTC Lemsip 2–3/day.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies. Seasonal hay fever symptoms.
- Social history and preventive care: Lives with partner and a dog; office manager. Alcohol: occasional (“odd cherry”). Smoking status not documented. Height 5′5″; weight 65 kg. Recent diabetes blood test ~3 weeks ago reported “normal.” Last BP check “a while ago,” stability unknown.

Examination:
- 
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not performed (telehealth).

Impression:
- Probable viral respiratory infection (described as “chest infection”) with upper respiratory symptoms; no current red flags reported. Higher vigilance advised given diabetes.

Plan:
- Monitoring: Obtain a thermometer and check temperature at home.
- Symptomatic care: May continue Lemsip (contains acetaminophen/paracetamol); avoid taking any additional acetaminophen-containing products concurrently. Avoid cough syrup during daytime; may use a small amount at night if cough prevents sleep.
- Expected course: Viral infections typically improve over 1–2 weeks; cough can persist longer.
- Safety-net: Seek medical review if fever persists >37.5–38°C, cough worsens, develops heavy purulent sputum, any hemoptysis, new nosebleeds, shortness of breath, or chest pain. If not improving or worsening, antibiotics may be considered.
- Chronic disease care: Maintain regular diabetes and blood pressure checkups with GP. Patient does not currently check blood sugars at home.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Objective vitals (including temperature and oxygen saturation); smoking status; full medication doses/routes/frequencies; type of diabetes; immunization status (e.g., flu/COVID, pneumococcal); recent BP readings; availability of home glucose monitoring not established for use.
- Internal conflicts: None noted; lisinopril dose reported as “two hundred” with units/frequency not documented (unclear).
- Transcript quality: Minor inaudible/unclear sections; overall adequate for clinical documentation.
